app.title: SeedVision AI | Seed Quality Grader
app.summary: A person picks a trained classifier and uploads one seed photograph, or chooses a demo sample. They get a predicted quality grade with its confidence, a bar chart of the probability for each class, a warning when the model is uncertain, and a three-panel Grad-CAM view whose target class they can change. On a separate review page they go through photographs grouped by physical specimen. For each specimen they see every view side by side and can run an image-quality screen and model suggestion that only advise. They then save one label, status, confidence, reviewer and diagnostic note for all of that specimen's views in the staging manifest, which is backed up before each save and can be reverted or restored. A benchmark page sets the trained architectures against each other with metrics, confusion matrices and calibration plots.

task.text: Grade a seed photograph into a fixed set of defect classes, show which image regions drove the call, and have a person confirm the label of each multi-view specimen before it is admitted to a training set.

data.text: Photographs of single seeds, grouped into physical specimens with several views each, listed in a staging manifest. Each specimen has a candidate defect class from a fixed four-class taxonomy, a review status, a confidence, a reviewer and notes. Alongside these are model checkpoints and their saved evaluation metrics.
data.item: a physical seed specimen photographed from several angles, or one seed photograph

stage.text: verifying labels on incoming specimen photographs before they join a training set, with model checks alongside

mechanism.text: A sidebar radio switches between pages. The analysis page runs the selected checkpoint on one image and shows grade metrics, a probability bar chart and an original / heatmap / overlay triplet. The staging page shows a specimen picker over summary counts, then a gallery of the chosen specimen's views, an optional advisory panel, a review form that writes to every view at once, and revert and restore controls.

field.text: CNN image classification with Grad-CAM attribution for seed quality grading in agricultural computer vision

workflow.name: confirm the label of each multi-view specimen before it enters a training set

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Metric cards count specimens, photographic views, and approved and pending views, and warn about image files missing from disk.
A specimen dropdown shows each specimen's status, label and view count. Choosing one opens an information card and a gallery of all its views side by side, with pixel sizes.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: An opt-in checkbox runs blur, brightness and contrast screening, near-duplicate hashing across the views, and an optional class suggestion from a compatible checkpoint. It shows whether the views agree and gives an advisory recommendation, but never sets the label.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: The review form sets a target defect label from the fixed taxonomy, a review status, the reviewer's confidence, the reviewer's identity and morphological notes, and saves them to every view of the specimen. Low confidence keeps the specimen pending.
Each save first backs up the manifest. One button reverts the current specimen to pending; ticking a confirmation box enables a button that restores the whole manifest from the backup.

On the analysis page the person picks a checkpoint and uploads or chooses one image. It is validated and graded, with confidence, latency, an uncertainty advisory, a softmax bar chart, and a Grad-CAM triplet whose target class can be changed.

A benchmark table and comparison chart cover all architectures. Choosing one architecture shows its accuracy, macro F1, calibration error (ECE), latency, confusion matrices and reliability curve, with a banner saying whether the run is real, unverified or synthetic.

distinctive: Labels are given per physical specimen, not per image: one decision is written to every photographic view of the same seed, so views cannot split across labels or data partitions.
Model and image-quality help is strictly advisory: automatic approval is disabled by policy, and views whose suggestions conflict are flagged for human inspection.
Near-duplicate views of one specimen are detected by image hashing and flagged as a single observation, not independent evidence.
Grad-CAM can explain any class hypothesis, not only the top prediction, so the person can see what would support an alternative grade.
Checkpoints and evaluation runs are tagged by data provenance (real, synthetic or unverified), and the provenance is shown next to every metric.
